rv.q: Shayok Misha Chowdhury's 'Public Obscenities,' is an absolute stunner.
The production elements come together seamlessly on the larger stage at TFANA.
The play is challenging as the first long extended scene is mainly in Bangla, the language of Kolkata, without supertitles.
Chowdhury is redefining what constitutes public and private obscenity.
'Public Obscenities' is one of those slow-boil plays that feels like it's building to something spectacular, but never actually does.
A wonderful production with a strong cast and fabulous design
The exotic setting and the overall authenticity of the expertly acted proceedings help to make a visit worthwhile.
